Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers. Fix a finite genuine integral parabolic central summand $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, with its finite highest-weight structure from [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Connectedness is not required. Write $(\Lambda,\preceq)$ for its label poset, $L_\lambda$ for its simples, $\Delta_\lambda$ for its generalized standards, and $\nabla_\lambda=D\Delta_\lambda$ for its costandards. The duality $D$ is exact, contravariant and simple-preserving.

The projective cover $P_\lambda$ and injective envelope $I_\lambda=DP_\lambda$ have exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow K_\lambda\longrightarrow P_\lambda\longrightarrow\Delta_\lambda\longrightarrow0,\qquad0\longrightarrow\nabla_\lambda\longrightarrow I_\lambda\longrightarrow C_\lambda\longrightarrow0,$$
where $K_\lambda$ has a finite standard flag with labels strictly greater than $\lambda$, and $C_\lambda=DK_\lambda$ has a finite costandard flag with such labels. Generally $I_\lambda$ is larger than $\nabla_\lambda$. Standards have simple heads, costandards simple socles, and their composition labels are $\preceq\lambda$. In this split setting,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\mathbb C,\qquad\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,\nabla_\mu)=0\quad(j>0),$$
and BGG reciprocity is $(P_\lambda:\Delta_\mu)=[\nabla_\mu:L_\lambda]=[\Delta_\mu:L_\lambda]$. Higher Ext vanishing is justified below from the standard-kernel sequences and the local Hom/$\operatorname{Ext}^1$ statement.

A **finite standard flag** of $N$ is a finite chain $0=N_0\subset N_1\subset\cdots\subset N_r=N$ with sections $\Delta_{\lambda_i}$; a **finite costandard flag** has sections $\nabla_{\lambda_i}$. The zero object has the empty flag. Write $\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $\mathcal F(\nabla)$ for the corresponding full subcategories. They are exact categories with the short exact sequences inherited from $\mathcal C$, closed under finite sums, extensions and direct summands. Their flag multiplicities are independent of the chosen flag and satisfy
$$(N:\Delta_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(N,\nabla_\lambda),\qquad(M:\nabla_\lambda)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta_\lambda,M).$$
For arbitrary objects of the fixed finite summand, the equivalent homological criteria are
$$\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^j(N,\nabla_\lambda)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\},$$
$$\mathcal F(\nabla)=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda\}=\{M:\operatorname{Ext}^j(\Delta_\lambda,M)=0\text{ for all }\lambda,j>0\}.$$
The duality exchanges the two flag categories. A **tilting object** belongs to their intersection.

An indecomposable tilting object is **normalized at** $\lambda$, and written $T_\lambda$, if it has an inclusion $\Delta_\lambda\hookrightarrow T_\lambda$ whose cokernel is standard-filtered by labels strictly smaller than $\lambda$. Its bottom standard occurs once and $\lambda$ is its unique maximal composition-support label. Such an object, when it exists, is unique up to isomorphism. Existence and classification are supplied later; they are not used to prove the criteria. For a lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing $\lambda$, this same object is normalized tilting in the corresponding Serre subcategory; it is unchanged by the truncation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n$, with its upper Borel and Cartan, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the standard parabolic of the tableau column sizes $n_1,\ldots,n_l$. Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}=\bar{\mathfrak l}\oplus\bar{\mathfrak u}$ be the standard parabolic with these block sizes reversed. Set $\alpha_i(\zeta)=0$ on the simple Levi roots and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ on the remaining simple roots, and grade by $\operatorname{ad}\zeta$. Thus
$$\mathfrak g_0=\bar{\mathfrak l},\qquad \mathfrak g_{>0}=\bar{\mathfrak u},\qquad \mathfrak g_{<0}=\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-}.$$
Degrees greater than one are retained. Put $U=U(\mathfrak g)$, $B=U(\bar{\mathfrak p})$, $N=U(\bar{\mathfrak u}^{-})$, and $\gamma=2\rho_{\mathfrak g}-2\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak l}}$, a character of $\bar{\mathfrak l}$ extended by zero to $\bar{\mathfrak u}$. For a graded vector space $V$, write $V^{\#}=\bigoplus_d(V_{-d})^*$ and
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(V,W)=\bigoplus_d\operatorname{Hom}^d(V,W).$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}^d$ consists of maps homogeneous of degree $d$; the direct sum allows only finitely many degrees. These conventions are essential.

(1) The algebraic space $S=N^{\#}\otimes B$ has commuting left and right $U$-actions and identifications
$$S\cong N^{\#}\otimes_N U\cong U\otimes_N N^{\#}.$$
Its left action is obtained from the restricted coinduction model
$$S\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(U,\mathbb C_\gamma\otimes B).$$
No completion of $S$ is taken. With $P$ and $Q$ the projections of $\mathfrak g$ to $\mathfrak g_{\ge0}$ and $\mathfrak g_{<0}$, respectively, the polarization trace governing normal ordering is
$$\omega(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_{\ge0}}(P\operatorname{ad}XQ\operatorname{ad}YP-P\operatorname{ad}YQ\operatorname{ad}XP)=\gamma_0([X,Y]),$$
where $\gamma_0$ is zero outside degree zero. In particular, for $X\in\mathfrak g_1$ and $Y\in\mathfrak g_{-1}$ this is $\gamma([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g_0}(\operatorname{ad}X\operatorname{ad}Y)$, not the full adjoint-composition trace.

(2) On graded $U$-modules free over $N$ of finite graded rank, $T=S\otimes_U-$ is an exact equivalence onto the graded $U$-modules cofree over $N$ of finite graded rank. Its inverse is $H=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_U(S,-)$; finite graded rank means a finite sum of grading shifts of $N$, respectively $N^{\#}$. In this restricted sense
$$\underline{\operatorname{End}}_N(N^{\#})\cong N^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This equality is not an assertion about unrestricted endomorphisms: for $N=\mathbb C[x]$ with $\deg x=-1$, the unrestricted ring is $\mathbb C[\![x]\!]$.

(3) With the principal contragredient action $(Xf)(v)=-f(Xv)$ on the restricted dual, $\Phi(M)=(S\otimes_U M)^{\#}$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of the finite generalized-standard flag category for $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its own opposite. On a finite-dimensional simple $\bar{\mathfrak l}$-module $E$,
$$\Phi(\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(E))\cong\Delta^{\bar{\mathfrak p}}(\mathbb C_{-\gamma}\otimes E^*).$$
The parabolic in this formula is unchanged.

(4) Let $c(X)=-w_0X^{\mathsf T}w_0$, which carries the upper Borel to itself and reverses the Levi blocks, and set $\Psi=c^*\Phi$. For a lower-bounded tableau shape set $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and use the concatenated ordinary highest-weight reading $a_i$, with each column read from top to bottom in strictly decreasing order, and $\lambda_{A,i}=a_i+i-1$. The source reading is the reversed sequence of columns, without reversing positions within a column. Then
$$\Psi:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(\Delta)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A).$$
This is an exact contravariant equivalence. It preserves the tableau label and the corresponding central-character summands, including the scalar central coordinate, and the reverse-column label order is opposite to the target order. More explicitly its weight map is
$$\lambda\longmapsto w_0w_{\bar J}\lambda+2w_0\rho_{\bar{\mathfrak u}}.$$

(5) For restricted BGG transpose duality $D$, the composite $F=D\Psi$ is an exact covariant equivalence $\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$ with $F(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\nabla(A)$.

For category-$\mathcal O$ modules these constructions use finite weight spaces and the finite direct sum of $\zeta$-eigenvalue cosets modulo $\mathbb Z$. Internal homogeneous Hom becomes the $\zeta$-locally finite part of Hom, and the dual is the weight-restricted dual. No equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or unrestricted completed Hom spaces is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every dominant
integral weight $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$, the character of the finite-dimensional
simple module $L(\lambda)$ is
$$\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=A(\lambda+\rho)\cdot A(\rho)^{-1}=\Bigl(\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}e^{w(\lambda+\rho)}\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(e^{\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})\Bigr),$$
the quotient being taken in the completed character ring $\mathcal R$ of
[[def-completed-formal-character-ring-for-downward-cones]], where
$A(\rho)$ is invertible with inverse
$e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$
([[thm-weyl-denominator-identity]],
[[lem-geometric-series-invertibility-in-the-completed-character-ring]]). No
quotient of ordinary functions is intended before this formal cancellation is
justified.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] only for the quantum-bar suppliers. In a finite type-$A$ natural tensor space, write $s$ for the source parameter, $a w$ for the right place action, $w_a$ for the shortest sorting permutation, $d_a=w_a^{-1}$, $K$ for the stabilizer of the weakly increasing sorted tuple, $w_K$ for its longest element, and $w_0$ for the full longest permutation. Let $L_b=\sum_a U_{a,b}(s)M_a$ be the positive-source ordinary-bar chart and $M_b=\sum_a D_{a,b}(s)L_a$ its inverse. Then
$$U_{a,b}(s)=(-s)^{\ell(w_b)-\ell(w_a)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_az,w_b}(s^{-2}),$$
$$D_{a,b}(s)=s^{\ell(w_b)-\ell(w_a)}P_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(s^{-2}).$$
Coefficients vanish outside the indicated Bruhat intervals. For decreasing-column wedge tensors in either factor order, the ordinary-bar embedding is
$$\iota(M_B)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}M_{a(C)},\qquad \iota(L_A)=L_{a(A)}.$$
Consequently the wedge inverse coefficient is
$$d_{A,B}(s)=\sum_{C\sim_{\mathrm{col}}B}(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}D_{a(A),a(C)}(s).$$
Here $\ell(B,C)$ is the number of within-column adjacent swaps from the decreasing reading. These identities are independent of category $\mathcal O$ and of linkage or simple-label identification.

derivations.claim: **The actual normalized projective image.** Fix one finite highest-weight central summand and a label $B$, and put $X(B)=\Psi(P^{\bar p}(B))$. The source projective has its highest-weight exact sequence $0\to\bar K(B)\to P^{\bar p}(B)\to\bar\Delta(B)\to0$, with a finite standard flag on $\bar K(B)$ using strictly higher source labels. Exact contravariance of $\Psi$ gives $0\to\Delta(B)\to X(B)\to\Psi\bar K(B)\to0$. Order reversal makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $B$. Thus this is an actual normalized bottom inclusion, and $\Delta(B)$ occurs once. The endomorphism ring of $X(B)$ is opposite to the local ring of its source projective cover, so $X(B)$ is indecomposable.

**The CWZ parameter, coproduct and ordered labels.** In the two-wedge convention of Cheng–Wang–Zhang, write $q$ for their parameter and $K_a$ for their toral generator. The exact transport to [F4] is $q\mapsto s^{-1}$, $K_a\mapsto D_a^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$, and $K_f\mapsto M_f$ for the same two decreasing columns in the same left/right order. Their natural eigenvalue $q^{\delta_{ab}}$ becomes $s^{-\delta_{ab}}$, the eigenvalue of $D_a^{-1}$. The toral relations and the $E/F$ commutator agree because both numerator and denominator of the toral fraction reverse sign. Their coproducts are $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes K_{a+1}K_a^{-1}$ and $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+K_aK_{a+1}^{-1}\otimes F_a$; these become exactly $1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$ and $F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$ of [F4]. Thus reciprocal parameter substitution alone is accompanied by toral inversion, and no reversal of tensor factors or tableau entries is used. The quantum Serre coefficients are unchanged under reciprocation, and the two bars agree on coefficients and generators: both fix $E_a,F_a$ and invert the torus. The displayed source coproduct and ordered factor actions are those of [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]. The ordered wedge basis has coefficient-one adjacent-entry replacement actions, so it identifies the elementary wedge factors; their relation on unordered wedges becomes $-s$, consistently with this transport. A swap of exclusive left $b>$ right $a$ gives a strictly smaller label in both orders, since the left prefix changes by the positive root $\delta_a-\delta_b$. Consequently the CWZ positive-$q$ triangular chart maps to the negative-$s^{-1}$ chart of $T$, not to the positive-$s$ chart of $L$.

**Tilting and an actual normalized dual flag.** For an extension $0\to X(B)\to Z\to\Delta(A)\to0$, the middle object is standard-filtered by extension closure. Inverting $\Psi$ turns it into an extension with the opposite projective as quotient, which splits. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(A),X(B))=0$ for every $A$, and the criterion of [F1] makes $X(B)$ costandard-filtered and therefore tilting. The object $DX(B)$ is also tilting and indecomposable; duality fixes simple classes, so all its composition labels are $\le B$ and $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le B$, $\Delta(B)$ is the maximal-labelled projective. The maximal standard trace proved in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] injects $\Delta(B)$ into the standard-filtered $DX(B)$ with quotient standard-filtered by strictly smaller labels: its multiplicity space has dimension $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. Thus the dual has an actual normalized bottom-standard sequence. Uniqueness of such indecomposable tiltings in [F1] gives $X(B)\cong DX(B)$. This normalization uses the proved maximal trace and does not follow from exchanging the kinds of flags alone.

**Local three-case calculation in the corrected chart.** For a column $S$ write $n_S(a)=\mathbf1_{a\in S}$ and omit a replacement term if it would collide. The transported coproduct gives $E_aM_{L,R}=M_{L,R(a+1\mapsto a)}+s^{n_R(a)-n_R(a+1)}M_{L(a+1\mapsto a),R}$ and $F_aM_{L,R}=M_{L(a\mapsto a+1),R}+s^{-n_L(a)+n_L(a+1)}M_{L,R(a\mapsto a+1)}$. Match exclusive pairs by increasing positive distance, deleting matched endpoints, and call the resulting set $\Sigma_f^+$. Distinct pairs at the same distance cannot share an endpoint, so this prescription is unambiguous. Choose the smallest left value $b=a+1$ that is a matched endpoint. If $a$ is absent on the left, let $h$ lower this $b$ to $a$ and apply $F_a$. If $a$ is present on the left, it must also occur on the right: otherwise its distance to the right partner of $b$ would be smaller, forcing it to be a matched left endpoint contrary to the choice of $b$. In this case let $h$ raise that right $a$ to $b$ and apply $E_a$. The matching rules then give three cases: when the lower left neighbor $a$ is shared, its pair endpoint in $h$ moves from $b$ to $a$ and all other pairs persist; when $a$ is absent on both sides the pair set persists with that endpoint lowered; when $a$ occurs only on the right, $h$ loses precisely the distance-one pair $(b,a)$. For every subset of the remaining pairs, the two displayed action formulas have coefficient one in the first two cases: if a selected pair moves the active letter to the other column, the two relevant occupation numbers agree. In the last case both columns of $h$ contain $a$ and neither contains $b$, so $F_aM_{h_\Sigma}=M_{f_\Sigma}+s^{-1}M_{f_{\Sigma\cup\{(b,a)\}}}$. No wedge sorting sign enters, since an adjacent integer replacement either preserves its sorted position or is zero on collision.

**The opposite BGG coefficient identity.** From the tilting nature and maximal support of $X(B)$, every multiplicity can be computed as $(X(B):\Delta(A))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(X(B),\nabla(A))$. Applying the exact contravariant $\Psi$ to the finite standard flag of $\bar P(B)$ reverses its order but preserves the multiplicities of its corresponding standard sections. Opposite BGG reciprocity therefore gives $(X(B):M(A))=(\bar P(B):\bar M(A))=[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]$, the opposite parabolic composition coefficient.

**Bar-fixed pair formula and coefficient.** The predecessor procedure in step 2.2 terminates: $\sum L-\sum R$ decreases by one at each predecessor, all entries remain in the finite interval between the original smallest and largest entries, and both column sizes are fixed. At its terminal tuple there is no positive exclusive pair; in the fixed union/intersection fiber this is the unique minimal label, so its monomial is fixed by the triangular bar of [F4]. Apply the recorded $E_a,F_a$ in reverse predecessor order; they are bar-fixed. The subset calculation of step 2.2 proves inductively that the resulting bar-fixed vector is $U_f=\sum_{\Sigma\subseteq\Sigma_f^+}s^{-|\Sigma|}M_{f_\Sigma}$. The empty subset gives $M_f$, every nonempty subset gives a lower label, and disjoint exclusive endpoints make distinct subsets give distinct tableaux. Thus $U_f$ has precisely the negative-chart triangular condition of $T_f$, and uniqueness in [F4] gives $U_f=T_f$. In particular every single greedy-pair coefficient is $s^{-1}$ and specializes to $1$. This supplies the local proof in the correct chart; it does not identify a positive-$s$ fixed vector with the negative-chart canonical family.

**The independent tensor/wedge bridge and opposite flag.** Apply [[lem-finite-type-a-tensor-hecke-bars-and-complementary-coefficient-charts]] before making any categorical identification. Its tensor generators act at $v=s^{-1}$, its positive chart transports to the sign module by $G_i=-H_i$ at $v=s$, and its complementary representative is $w_Kd(A)w_0$. The proved inverse tensor coefficient is $s^{\ell(w_C)-\ell(w_A)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(s^{-2})$, so its value at $1$ is exactly the ordinary singular composition number in [F3]. The primitive ordinary-bar exterior embedding has coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(B,C)}$ on column permutations $C$ and sends the wedge $L_A$ to the ambient $L_{a(A)}$. Its signed inverse formula at $1$ therefore agrees term for term with finite Levi Weyl cancellation of the genuine generalized-standard character: $d_{A,B}(1)=[\Delta(B):L(A)]$. This uses character injectivity, and it keeps the equal-entry stabilizer separate from the column Levi. The helper proves the same transport for reversed factors; hence $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]$. At $s=1$ the ordinary tensor bar matrix is the identity (each adjacent exchange has correction $s^{-1}-s=0$), so the reverse form of [F4] has monomial Gram matrix $I$. The identity $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ now says that the monomial coefficient matrix of $T$ is the transpose inverse of the coefficient matrix of $\widetilde L$, namely $\widetilde d^{\mathsf T}$. Thus the coefficient of $M(A)$ in $T_B$ at $1$ is $\widetilde d_{B,A}(1)=[\bar\Delta(A):\bar L(B)]=(X(B):\Delta(A))$ by step 3.1. All sign, longest-element and reverse-factor transports have been proved independently of this linkage conclusion.

**Isolation of adjacent columns in a larger tensor.** If two tableaux have the same entries outside two adjacent columns, every tableau in the Bruhat interval between them has the same outer prefix weights, since dominance is antisymmetric on fixed total weight; parenthesizing the pair as one tensor factor, a positive transfer across an outer boundary strictly changes a prefix weight in the positive cone and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Hence the bar submatrix and, by triangular correction, the canonical coefficient between the two labelled monomials equal the two-column values of step 3.2.

**Genuine edges at $1$.** Specializing step 4.2 at $s=1$, a greedy-pair swap gives $(X(B):M(A))=1$ for the two labels connected by the swap: the corresponding standard factor occurs with multiplicity $1$ in the indecomposable tilting object $X(B)$. Since an indecomposable finite-length object cannot have composition factors in two different linkage blocks, and $M(A)$ has simple head $L(A)$ while the actual $\Delta(B)$ section of $X(B)$ supplies $L(B)$ as a composition factor, the labels $A$ and $B$ lie in the same actual linkage block. Opposite BGG gives $[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]=1$, and $\bar M(A)$ has head $\bar L(A)$, so the same edge connects the opposite labels.

**Connectivity of the binary tableau fiber.** Identify a tableau with the $0/1$ incidence matrix recording which entry values occur in each column; its row margins are entry multiplicities and its column margins are the heights $n_j$. At $s=1$ the displayed primitive exterior sum becomes the ordinary alternating column sum, and $D_{a,b}(1)=P_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(1)$ in both orders.

**Conclusion.** The generator and signed-chart steps prove the explicit generator/bar and signed antispherical transport; the reverse-position pairing and complementary-chart steps prove the spherical coefficient and its exact longest indices; the primitive exterior and wedge-chart steps prove the ordinary-bar embedding and signed inverse matrix in either ordered tensor. All constructions use finite tensor and Hecke data, independently of any categorical identification.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

This field assertion holds for arbitrary based pairs and does not imply integral action. Its integral and based assertion holds for exactly the admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients and direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs and products in finite Cartan type. For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently proved integral $\Theta$ action, not on field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.

In these cases: $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice; its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors modulo $q$, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; they form a genuine $A$-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple; the $q=0$ tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and the infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$, not an asserted bar containment in $L_0$, since semilinearity sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. Exact based integral and bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-$R$ braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action; the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable weight module $M$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], let $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P$ and $u\in L_\lambda$, and let $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ be the admissible $i$-string decomposition of $u$: the sum is finite, $u_n\in\ker E_i\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, and $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle h_i,\lambda+n\alpha_i\rangle$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]). Then:

(a) **Components lie in the lattice.** $u_n\in L\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ for every $n$.

(b) **Lattice string decomposition.** $L_\lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}\bigl(L_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}\cap\ker E_i\bigr)$, the sum being direct because admissible decompositions are unique; equivalently $L=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\tilde f_i^{\,n}(L\cap\ker E_i)$.

(c) **Single surviving component.** If $u+qL=0$ in $L_\lambda/qL_\lambda$, then $u_n\in qL$ for every $n$. If $u+qL\in B_\lambda$, then there is exactly one index $n_0$ with $u_{n_0}\notin qL$, and for it $u_{n_0}+qL\in B_{\lambda+n_0\alpha_i}$, $u\equiv F_i^{(n_0)}u_{n_0}\pmod{qL}$ and $u_{n_0}+qL=\tilde e_i^{\,n_0}(u+qL)$; in particular $n_0=\varepsilon_i(u+qL)$ ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]), and $\tilde e_iu$ and $\tilde f_iu$ are the residues of $F_i^{(n_0-1)}u_{n_0}$ and $F_i^{(n_0+1)}u_{n_0}$.

Everything is a statement about the fixed lattice $L$ and the operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$; no finite-dimensionality, bounded support, uniform nilpotence or choice principle is assumed. Here $F_i^{(-1)}u$ is interpreted as $0$, and $F_i^{(a+1)}u=0$ for a top of coroot weight $a$, so the final formulas include both finite-string endpoints.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

2.3 **The reverse-bar adjoint calculation.** Let $\omega$ be the linear anti-automorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$, $F_i\mapsto E_i$, $D_a\mapsto D_a$; reversing products preserves the toral mixed, commutator and Serre relations. Write $H_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The source coproduct has $\Delta E_i=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes H_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+H_i^{-1}\otimes F_i$. Put $\mathscr A=\mathrm{flip}\circ(\omega\otimes\omega)$. Direct substitution gives $\mathscr A\Delta E_i=F_i\otimes1+H_i\otimes F_i=\overline\Delta F_i$ and $\mathscr A\Delta F_i=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes H_i^{-1}=\overline\Delta E_i$; the toral coproduct is unchanged. Hence $\mathscr A\Delta(u)=\overline\Delta(\omega u)$ and $\mathscr A\overline\Delta(u)=\Delta(\omega u)$ on the generated algebra. Applying the anti-automorphism $\mathscr A$ to $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ gives $\mathscr A(\Theta)\overline\Delta(\omega u)=\Delta(\omega u)\mathscr A(\Theta)$. Its degree-zero term is one and flip with $E/F$ exchange preserves the positive-first/negative-second completion. The exact normalized uniqueness of [F3] therefore gives $\mathscr A(\Theta)=\Theta$. On each ordered minuscule wedge factor the $E_i,F_i$ matrices are mutually transpose and the $D_a$ matrices are diagonal, so transpose realizes $\omega$. Consequently transposing the original two-factor bar and reversing factors gives the reverse-factor bar in the same tableau labelling. The same statement for successive prefixes follows from the coproduct factorization and parenthesization independence of [F1], [F3]; thus $\widetilde B=B^{\mathsf T}$. In raw full-tensor labels this also reads $(\widetilde E_i)^{\mathsf T}=\overline{F_i}$, $(\widetilde F_i)^{\mathsf T}=\overline{E_i}$, where the bar acts on matrix coefficients and conjugates all toral weight powers. Finally $\widetilde B^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}B=B=\overline{B^{-1}}$, so $C(\widetilde\psi x,\psi y)=\overline{C(x,y)}$. This adjoint calculation uses the two ordinary tensor bars independently of charge transpose. [F1, F3, step 1.3, algebra]

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

The two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Every finite minuscule type-A tensor cut and either factor order. No category O or cellular-simple label identification; no whole-item acceptance stamp.

derivations.claim: **All reverse lower constituents.** Put $q=s^{-1}$ and use the reverse ordered tensor. Each elementary wedge subset factor is minuscule: for each root its nontrivial strings have length two, coefficients one, and its basis is its lower global basis at $q=0$ in the dictionary's toral convention $K_i=D_i^{-1}D_{i+1}$. The ground vector generates it. Apply [F1] to the finite product, not to just the ground constituent. Its raw reverse monomial $A_0(q)$-span is the lower tensor chart by [F2]; finite triangular correction produces the negative-source family $\widetilde T_A$ by uniqueness. Thus the reverse Laurent lattice and the zero/infinity charts have the simultaneous global basis $\widetilde T_A$.

**The actual sesquilinear dual and exchanged coefficient rings.** Define $H(x,y)=C(\widetilde\psi x,y)$ on reverse/original factors. It is coefficient-antilinear in $x$ and linear in $y$. From [F3], $H(\widetilde M_A,M_B)=\overline{C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)}=\delta_{AB}$, so its raw monomial Gram matrix is exactly $I$. Therefore the conjugate dual of the reverse $A_0(q)$-raw chart is exactly the original $A_0(s)$-raw chart: a coefficient $a(q)$ is conjugated to $a(q^{-1})=a(s)$, including denominators. Similarly the reverse infinity chart dualizes to the original infinity chart. On the global families $H(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$ because $\widetilde T_A$ is fixed. Hence the dual integral, zero and infinity lattices have respectively bases $L_A$ over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$, $A_0(s)$ and $A_\infty(s)$, and their common intersection is $\bigoplus_A\mathbb ZL_A$. This proves balancedness and identifies its ordinary bar with $\psi$ using the conjugate-bar identity of [F3]. It does not equate the two ordinary global bases.

**Upper operators and full tableau residues.** The matrix adjoints of [F3], with the conjugation in $H$, give $H(\widetilde F_ix,y)=H(x,E_iy)$ and $H(\widetilde E_ix,y)=H(x,F_iy)$. On a reverse divided string $v_k=F_i^{(k)}v_0$, $0\le k\le a$, let $u_k$ be its $H$-dual basis, retaining the full pairing on its multiplicity space. Then $E_iu_k=[k]_su_{k-1}$ and $F_iu_k=[a-k]_su_{k+1}$ by [F2] and $\overline{[m]_q}=[m]_s$. The upper string operators are the shifts $u_k\mapsto u_{k-1},u_{k+1}$, defined as the conjugate adjoints of the lower shifts. They preserve the dual charts from step 2.1 and their residues are the adjoints of the partial permutation matrices of the lower tensor crystal. Thus they give partial inverse tableau moves on every tensor residue, with the reverse factor order undone by the dual pairing. On a column the simultaneous $i,i+1$ occupations cancel; on the original left-to-right column word cancel $-+$, with $-$ an $i+1$-only column and $+$ an $i$-only column. The raising move takes the leftmost surviving $-$ and lowering takes the rightmost surviving $+$: this is the reverse lower tensor rule of [F2] read through the dual basis. Equalities follow from the lower rule's non-strict raising and strict lowering tests, so no equality case is changed by naming the chart upper. Both reciprocal charts have the corresponding upper operators.

**Endpoint divided powers and balanced uniqueness.** On the upper string $u_k$ of step 3.1, $E_i^{(k)}u_k=u_0$ and $E_i^{(k+1)}u_k=0$; thus if $E_i^{(n+1)}x=0$, then $E_i^{(n)}x=\tilde e_i^nx$, since all shorter components die. This is an identity on the sum of admissible strings, with its multiplicity spaces retained. If $x=L_A$ and $E_i^{(n+1)}x=0$, integrality of divided powers and preservation of both upper charts put $E_i^{(n)}x$ in their balanced intersection, with residue $\tilde e_i^nA$. Therefore it equals $L_{\tilde e_i^nA}$ when that residue is nonzero, and zero otherwise. Conversely suppose $\tilde e_i^{n+1}A=0$ but $E_i^{(n+1)}L_A\ne0$. Choose the maximal $m>n$ for which $E_i^{(m)}L_A\ne0$, possible by finite integrability. Applying the endpoint argument with $m$ gives a nonzero balanced vector with residue $\tilde e_i^mA=0$, contradicting injectivity in [F4]. Thus $E_i^{n+1}L_A=0$ iff $\varepsilon_i(A)\le n$.

**Adapted kernels, without assuming a tensor highest decomposition is based.** To exclude cancellation between global vectors outside a kernel, choose the largest $m$ occurring among the $\varepsilon_i(A)$ in a finite linear combination. Apply $E_i^{(m)}$. Step 4.1 sends its $m$-height terms to distinct top-labelled global vectors: partial inverse crystal strings imply that two labels at the same position have different top labels. Every lower-height term dies. Linear independence therefore forces all coefficients at that height to vanish if the combination is killed. Descend on $m$ to obtain the stated kernel span. The integral and chart kernels are exactly the spans of the same subset over their coefficient rings, because the global vectors are simultaneous bases. Hence all these kernel triples are balanced; quotienting by one such subset retains simultaneous bases and balancedness.

**The associated rank-one filtration.** At root weight $\lambda=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(A)\rangle$, a string of dimension $r$ has position $k=(r-1-\lambda)/2$. Thus the sum of strings with dimension at most $r$ at that weight is precisely $\ker E_i^{k+1}$, with the natural floor when parity requires it; by step 5.1 its global labels have $\varepsilon_i\le k$, equivalently $r_i\le r$. These weightwise spaces assemble into the rank-one submodule filtration. The associated quotient of dimension $r$ has simultaneous bases indexed by the labels $r_i(A)=r$, and is a sum of actual upper strings $u_0,\ldots,u_{r-1}$. Step 4.1 identifies the top vector of the position-$k$ global residue by $E_i^{(k)}L_A=L_{\tilde e_i^kA}$, modulo the shorter-string filtration. Consequently the position-$k$ vector is the upper normalized $u_k$, whose $E_i,F_i$ coefficients are exactly $[k]_s$ and $[r-1-k]_s$ by step 3.1. Identifying the next residue by partial inverse moves proves the two asserted leading-term equations, with all errors in shorter strings. This does not require a separately selected highest-weight decomposition of the full tensor module.

**Conclusion and factor orders.** Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 construct the full source upper triple and its tableau residue crystal by conjugate duality of the entire reverse lower tensor construction; steps 4.1 and 5.1 give balanced adapted kernels; step 6.1 gives the associated-string Chevalley normalization. Reversing the initially chosen factor order repeats the same construction, and finite cuts commute with all supported subset actions and triangular global lifts. Every claim therefore concerns the full finite tensor cuts and both ordered products, without any categorical simple-label assertion.
